findings.evidence: Prime/Discriminant/Basic.lean:125-126 `theorem odd_oddPrimeDiscriminant {p : ℕ} (hp : Odd p) : Odd (oddPrimeDiscriminant p)` — same prefix, `Odd` conclusion.
findings.fix: Either restate the conclusion as `Odd (∏ i ∈ s, oddPrimeDiscriminant (p i))` (keeping the name), or rename to `not_two_dvd_prod_oddPrimeDiscriminant` and fix the docstring.
findings.issue: `odd_prod_oddPrimeDiscriminant` states `¬ (2 : ℤ) ∣ ∏ i ∈ s, oddPrimeDiscriminant (p i)`, not `Odd (…)`; the docstring "A product of odd prime discriminants is odd" reinforces the wrong reading. The `odd_` prefix already denotes an `Odd` conclusion in this namespace.

findings.evidence: Naming conventions: hypotheses that must be described are separated by `of`. Repo precedent: Prime/Discriminants.lean:135 `primeDiscriminantRadicand_of_isEvenPrimeDiscriminant`, :225 `primeDiscriminantRadicand_mod_four_eq_one_of_odd`.
findings.fix: Rename to `isFundamentalDiscriminant_mul_prod_oddPrimeDiscriminant_of_isEvenPrimeDiscriminant` (or `isFundamentalDiscriminant_evenPrimeDiscriminant_mul_prod_oddPrimeDiscriminant`), following the repo's existing `_of_` convention for such hypotheses.
findings.issue: `isFundamentalDiscriminant_mul_prod_oddPrimeDiscriminant` names the left factor only as `mul`, so the name asserts more than the theorem: it holds only when `e` satisfies `IsEvenPrimeDiscriminant e`, which the name omits entirely.

summary: Two names misdescribe their statements: one advertises `Odd` while proving a non-divisibility, and one hides the even-prime-discriminant hypothesis behind a bare `mul_`. No notation is introduced; the rest of the names follow existing prime-discriminant precedent.
